text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former interior minister Mehmet Agar, who resigned over a security scandal, says he has secrets to keep until he dies.
- The armed forces are angered by criticism from Islamist politicians and media of the expulsion of devout Moslem officers from the military.
- Interrogation of underworld gang members sheds light on their involvement in various crimes from killing to drug smuggling.
- Interior Ministry inspectors investigating the murder of a casino entrepreneur ask for more authority as they say they have found shocking clues.
- President Suleyman Demirel demands that the prime minister accelerate investigations into a security scandal linking organised crime, police and the state.
- The Islamist-led government will not able to sell state property as the constitutional court annulled the relevant law.
- Turkey's customs union with the European Union maintains its problematic status a year after Ankara signed the accord.
- Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller is advised by senior members of her True Path Party (DYP) not to support the former interior minister, also a DYP deputy.
- Most of those expelled from the armed forces, who do not have a right to a pension, are having psychological problems.
